strokeOrderSource.variation: Both independent-form animations draw the pointed hooked head, descent, and deep bowl in one uninterrupted body-first stroke, then place the lower-left dot, the lower-right dot, and finally the lower-center dot: four strokes separated by three pen lifts. The adjacent prose identifies che as the jīm-series shape with three dots below the head and gives its ch sound. This learner path covers the independent form and fits the body-first, three-dot order to the course's vendored Noto Naskh fallback; Urdu is conventionally printed in Nastaliq, and the app's true Nastaliq face remains separate from this canonical script-data fallback.
